confirmedRegressions: The new path material averages to nearly flat grey in the actual GPU image. The small texels and weak normal encoding disappear under mip filtering.
Both curb lines contain default white meshes. The paving array was reduced to four materials but the curb index remained modulo eight.
Applied entrance leaves still read as bright thin gold cutouts instead of rounded carved wood with selective gilding.
The lantern proportions improved, but the surface is chalky and the cap has sparse moss.
Real leaf shadows now reach the foreground, but their broad dense coverage and flat crowns still need correction.

fourthPass.curb: Index uses paving.length. The mesh helper now rejects absent materials instead of silently accepting Three.js's default white material.
fourthPass.stoneSampling: Periodic multi-scale albedo, roughness and normal data now include visible mineral aggregates and pitting. Source normal red bytes span 62–194; the previous almost-neutral normals lost their detail in sampling.
fourthPass.stoneGeometry: Top faces are refined into actual continuous millimetre relief, with discontinuous moss rooted in the shared polygon joints.
fourthPass.gpuAudit: window.temple.info().surfaceAudit records the material map UUID and the compiled shader uniform map UUID after an actual frame. This needs checking in the root-managed GPU run.
fourthPass.carving: Convex closed leaf bodies with carved midribs replace flat front faces. Gilding occupies small veins and selected leaves; repeated small eave rings are reduced.
fourthPass.plants: Crown clusters gain vertical depth and per-leaf colour variation. Near-path crown density is lower, and lotus petals become wider, shorter cupped forms.
fourthPass.status: Fourth source pass committed; actual GPU visual acceptance remains pending.
